Granger House in Eastern Iowa offers year-round paranormal activity

The Granger House Victorian Museum in Marion, Iowa, is home to ghostly activity and offers Halloween-themed events for visitors.

MARION, Iowa —

Halloween is just around the corner, but for one house in Eastern Iowa, the haunts are year-round.

The Granger House Victorian Museum, which features 1800s Victorian architecture, was home to Earl and Dora Granger and their family for more than 140 years. A Granger family member lived there continuously until the last one died in 1969, KCRG-TV reports.

Volunteers who keep the home standing said the family never actually left.

Volunteer Vicki Noah said she believes the spirits are happy their home is still being cared for.

"Footsteps, giggling, humming, singing, and I swear I'm not crazy," Noah said. "There was one night I was here by myself, and I heard plain as day, 'Vicki!' And I said, 'What?' And then I was like, I'm here by myself, and then I said, no, you're really not here by yourself. I'm never here by myself."

On Tuesday night, a group of beginners used the Granger House Victorian Museum for their first lesson in paranormal investigation, where spirits were reportedly lively.

Participants learned to use equipment such as dowsing rods and an EMF meter before stepping inside.

The most active area of the house was a little boy's room on the upper floor.

Participants spent time getting to know the spirits' personalities and said goodbye to them at the end of the night.

The museum is offering Halloween-themed events in the coming weeks, including scavenger hunts and trick-or-treating. Information on those opportunities can be found here.
